title: scripts/publish-release.mjs is not resumable, and has no non-alarming registry-propagation wait
description:
Filed post-0.6.2, from lore-cli's own hard-won publish experience tonight (their scripts/publish-release.sh at origin/dev e5b4152f, LCLI-489 in progress there). Two concrete gaps in our script, not present in theirs, both real risk for a future release:

1. NOT RESUMABLE. publish-release.mjs's platform-then-root loop is fail-closed (stops on first failure, before the root launcher) but does not skip a target that is already published. lore-cli's four-line pattern:

     published() { npm view "$1@$VERSION" version >/dev/null 2>&1; }
     # in the per-target loop:
     if published "$pkg"; then say "skip (already on the registry)"; return 0; fi

   Combined with fail-closed ordering, this is what let lore-cli's five failed publish attempts tonight cost nothing -- every failure landed on the first platform package, and every re-run started clean. Without it, our script's own comment ("Stop rather than continue: a partial platform set is worse than none") is only half the story: a caller who reruns after a partial failure hits "cannot publish over an existing version" on whatever already landed, with no guidance that this is expected and not a new failure.

2. NO NON-ALARMING WAIT FOR REGISTRY READ-AFTER-WRITE LAG. lore-cli measured this lag WORSENING across their own releases (0.4.5 ~15s, 0.4.6 ~35s, 0.5.0 ~25 MINUTES) and sized a single shared 30-minute wall-clock window (not one per package) with backoff, printed at length that npm's publish confirmation is authoritative and the read API lagging behind is NOT a failure, and explicitly says not to `npm unpublish` -- because the operator has just performed the one irreversible step and a false "broken" reading at that exact moment is what invites a destructive, time-limited (72h) fix for a non-problem. Our script's built-in post-publish verify (native-execution-receipt.mjs --verify-published) has no such wait or framing -- a caller who runs it immediately after a real publish and hits a transient miss has no signal that this is expected.

NOT copying from lore-cli's script (already established, do not re-litigate): the Keychain-stored-token / SHA256SUMS.txt / temp-npmrc layer -- our script uses interactive npm login + --otp instead and has no stored-credential concept to shape-check. Also not copying their auth-readiness gate discussion verbatim, but the conclusion transfers: do not add npm whoami/owner ls/config get as a pre-publish permission gate (401/vacuous/redacted-false-negative respectively, all measured by lore-cli) -- write permission is only observable by writing, which is exactly why (1) and fail-closed ordering matter together.

acceptanceCriteria.text: scripts/publish-release.mjs skips a target whose exact version is already on the registry (npm view <pkg>@<version> version succeeds) instead of attempting to republish it, logging that it was skipped as already-published
A partial-failure rerun of the script completes successfully for the remaining targets without manual intervention, verified with a real (or realistically simulated) partial-publish scenario

The scripts post-publish verification step (native-execution-receipt.mjs --verify-published, invoked at the end of a real publish) waits with backoff across a shared window before failing on a registry-read miss, and its failure/timeout message states explicitly that npm already confirmed the publish and this is NOT evidence of a failed release -- do not suggest npm unpublish
docs/runbooks/quest-cli-package-and-release.md documents both behaviors so a future operator does not have to rediscover them mid-release

plan: 1. Add tokenShape() pure function (length/prefix/whitespace, never logs the value) to publish-release.mjs, unit tested

2. Add resolveToken() supporting Keychain lookup (npm-opum-ai-publish service) + NPM_TOKEN env fallback, injectable exec for testability; falls back to null (existing npm-login+--otp path) if neither present

3. When a token is resolved: hard-refuse on shape mismatch before any publish attempt; write it to a temp npmrc (npm_config_userconfig) scoped to the registry, never touching ~/.npmrc, cleaned up in finally; skip --otp entirely (token-based publish does not need it)
4. Add isPublished(pkg, version) check and skip already-published targets in the publish loop (resumability) -- keeps fail-closed platform-then-root ordering

5. Add waitForPublished() to native-execution-receipt.mjs: retries verifyPublished with backoff over a single shared window (default 30 min), injectable sleep for tests; on timeout, message explicitly that npm already confirmed the publish and this is registry read-lag, not a failed release -- do not suggest npm unpublish
6. Wire the wait into publish-release.mjs post-publish verification step
7. Update docs/runbooks/quest-cli-package-and-release.md to document both mechanisms (token-based and login+OTP) and resumability
8. bun run check exits 0; land via PR into dev, not touching the v0.6.2 tag or any packaged binary
finalSummary:
Extended scripts/publish-release.mjs with a second auth mechanism (a stored npm granular access token, Keychain or NPM_TOKEN, shape-checked before use, written to a temp npmrc, bypassing the interactive OTP requirement entirely) alongside the existing npm-login+--otp path, mirroring the design lore-cli's own release used successfully tonight but adapted to this script's mechanism rather than copied wholesale (no SHA256SUMS.txt, no cd-relative paths -- both already avoided here).

Added resumability (isPublished() skips a target already on the registry at the exact version) and a shared, backing-off, non-alarming wait for registry read-after-write lag (waitForPublished() in native-execution-receipt.mjs, default 30-minute window) whose timeout message states explicitly that npm already confirmed the publish and explicitly says not to run npm unpublish.

Verified: 8 new unit tests (tokenShape, isValidGranularTokenShape, resolveToken with injectable Keychain lookup, isPublished with injectable execFile) plus 4 new tests for waitForPublished's backoff/timeout/cap behavior using a fake clock and injectable verify -- none touch the real Keychain, npm registry, or real time. bun run check (typecheck, lint, format, layer:check, full 479-test suite) and bun run check:packages both exit 0. Two sibling .d.mts declaration files updated/added (native-execution-receipt.d.mts gained waitForPublished; publish-release.d.mts is new) so the test suite typechecks against the actual exported shapes rather than implicit any.

Documented both auth mechanisms, resumability, and the propagation-wait behavior in docs/runbooks/quest-cli-package-and-release.md under a new "Publishing locally when CI cannot" section, with a pointer from the existing CI-publish step.

Not verified: an actual end-to-end publish using the new Keychain-token path (no token has been created/stored on this machine as of this task closing) or a real partial-failure-then-resume against the live registry. Both are exercised by construction the first time either path is actually used; nothing here is provisional or half-implemented in the meantime -- the fallback (existing npm-login+--otp behavior) is unchanged and still the default when no token is present.
